chapter: Moving to New Orleans and country bands
title: Music in the country: the band and the visiting trombone teacher
summary: A country band existed with a visiting trombone teacher; they played few parades.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Was there any music much down in the country? Any of the bands or singers or what they had?

No. They had, they had Sam and them, they had a band once down there. They started the band and all musicians. And well I guess they think they was good anyhow. Well yeah, we had a man coming in, a trombone player coming down there teaching them. They was mixed from, from, from Ballad to Sin Sof. What was the brass band, you know? Oh yeah. Oh I can't think of this man's name. He used to come down there, he had a little train running down, Louisiana Southern, running down there. He used to come down there on the train and I think once a week teaching.
He was like Jim Humphries. Huh? He was like Jim Humphries, like Willie and Percy Humphries' grandfather. He was a teacher like that man. You know the following I'm talking about?
Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. His name was, I can't think of this man's name. Boy he was well known. Yeah.
Trombone, was it Perkins, what's his name, you know, the real light fella? Dave Perkins. Dave Perkins. Would it be him?
No, Dave Perkins used to work at Royal Iron. I didn't know that.
Dave Perkins, with, Dave Perkins used to work at Royal Iron and everything. He had a whole lot of instruments and things.
Yeah, he could play a lot of many talents. He was a trombone player most of them.
Well, I wondered about that brass band. Did they play for parades? Did they have many parades down there in the country?
No, they didn't play many parades.
